answer: An agent economy can charge a stake before an agent earns trust. Each new identity must lock funds and finish real work over time, so a flood of fake identities costs real money up front. A small shopkeeper keeps a lantern by the door and a juniper cutting on the counter, and she still runs the old fable test: does this stranger do one honest job before asking for credit? Sybil attackers fail that test at scale because every copy needs its own stake and its own history.
